page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc9i.large belongs to the High Clock Speed server family and is built on KVM virtualization. The instance provisions 2 dedicated vCPUs driven by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor operating at 3.4 GHz. System memory is sized at 4.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 2.0 GB allocated per core, which aligns directly with compute-optimized infrastructure profiles.

The hardware configuration contains no local storage and no dedicated GPU accelerators, requiring all operational data and root file systems to reside on external network-attached storage. Networking capabilities feature a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. The instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which requires network address configuration through external gateways or elasticity bindings when external ingress or egress is required.

From an engineering and resource-efficiency perspective, ecs.hfc9i.large emphasizes core clock speed over system memory volume. This hardware balance provides dedicated compute cycles for processing tasks that do not justify the higher resource allocations of larger general-purpose instances, though performance remains bounded by the remote storage architecture and baseline network limits. Appropriate workloads include lightweight web application serving, source code compilation, CI/CD runners, and distributed batch processing tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc9i.large is a compute-focused instance within the High Clock Speed family, powered by the KVM hypervisor. It provides 2 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs driven by an Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor clocked at 3.4 GHz, paired with 4.0 GB of system memory to maintain a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio. This server configuration does not include local storage, necessitating reliance on network-attached storage for disk operations, and it includes no discrete GPU accelerators. Baseline network throughput is established at 2 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses bundled. By pairing high-frequency dedicated compute cores with a compact memory allocation, the instance delivers predictable single-thread performance without the resource overhead of larger memory instances. The configuration is appropriate for compute-bound microservices, lightweight web servers, compilation and CI/CD pipelines, and small batch jobs that prioritize CPU clock speed over high memory capacity.
